questions: Did the final unseen-track design complete, and at what progress and completion_time?
Did steering_oscillation stay below 0.16 on every development track with the final kp?
Did line_loss_events stay at or below one per run on each track?
Which track ends off track first, and at what progress?
feedback_request.what_to_report: Per track (oval, s-bend, slalom): completion, progress, completion_time, rms_error, max_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation, control_effort, controller_errors. Also the kp used and the progress achieved on the unseen track.

intent: Freeze the best measured geometry (iteration 10) for the final race: seven contiguous 16 mm sensors at x = ±0.048 m, y = 0.08 m, wheel_track 0.085 m, mass 0.8 kg, radius 0.03 m, body 0.12 × 0.16 m. The Integrator should control oscillation through kp, not geometry. Expected: s-bend progress about 0.17, oval about 0.18, slalom oscillation below 0.16 and line loss at about one event per run on the s-bend and slalom.
learning: Across iterations 0 to 10, the binding failures were sensing footprint (fixed by 16 mm contiguous sensors at ±0.048 m), forward lead (plateaued at y = 0.07 to 0.08 m), and turn gain (track width 0.12 to 0.085 m gave steady gains until steering oscillation approached 0.16). Pitch widening, mass reduction and body width did not help. Future geometry work should test forward lead and track width jointly with kp, not each in isolation.
rationale: This is the final iteration, so I am choosing the geometry with the best measured evidence rather than testing a new step. Iteration 10 (wheel_track 0.085 m, all other geometry as iteration 9) scored 63.41, the best result so far. It met the decision rule I set in iteration 9: s-bend progress rose from 0.1675 to 0.1686 (oval 0.174 to 0.180), and slalom steering_oscillation stayed below 0.16 at 0.1569. Line loss stayed at one event per run on the s-bend and slalom, so sensing is not the limit. The one warning is that s-bend steering_oscillation averaged 0.1617, just over the 0.16 trigger, with line loss unchanged. Under the pre-agreed rule, that calls for the Integrator to reduce kp, not for a geometry change. Narrowing the track further (to 0.08 m) would add turn gain and push oscillation past the trigger on the slalom with no clear progress evidence, and the unseen final track has a different shape, so I do not take that risk. Sensing (seven contiguous 16 mm sensors at x = ±0.048 m, y = 0.08 m), mass 0.8 kg, wheel radius 0.03 m and body 0.12 × 0.16 m are all held at their tested values. Body width cannot improve the off-track limit, which is 0.06 m at any allowed width. I expect this layout to hold or slightly improve on the development tracks, with the final race depending mainly on the Integrator's kp choice for oscillation.
